Hi all

Thanks for the context. High-level proposal below plus an attached eval plan (reranker-eval-plan.md).

1) Integration patterns
- Option A (recommended for speed): Redwood ranking endpoint (POST /v1/rank) that accepts retrieved doc candidates + optional embeddings. This keeps scoring server-side and minimises network hops.
- Option B: Client-side scoring via SDK where you push embeddings and get per-document scores; useful if CoreHealth wants full control over embeddings build.

SDK & Auth
- Use server-side API keys with restricted scopes for scoring. We recommend rotating keys via your KMS and limiting to the reranker endpoint.
- Example header: Authorization: Bearer <RESTRICTED_RERANK_KEY>

Routing / Deployment
- For initial POC, route to our hosted tier (shared pool) but with reserved capacity if accuracy/latency needs persist. Given their QPS (20-80), hosted pool should be fine for eval. If p95 latency needs lower than 150ms we should propose a Dedicated pool.

Ranking API params (suggested defaults)
- top_k: default 10, sweep over [3,5,10,20] for eval
- return_scores: true
- score_threshold: optional, start with null (no filter)
- embeddings_input: optional JSONL with per-doc vectors; if not provided we run text-only encoder

Evaluation metrics and plan
- Primary: NDCG@5 and MRR@10
- Secondary: Recall@k and Precision@5, and a simple decision threshold test to estimate deflection improvement
- Latency: measure p50/p95 per-request scoring time (separate from retrieval time)
- Plan: run 2k queries against current BM25 baseline and our reranker across top_k sweep. Produce an NDCG/MRR table with 95% bootstrap CIs.

Top_k tuning guidance
- For many knowledge-base use cases, NDCG improvements saturate around top_k=5-10. If latency is tight, prefer top_k=5; if you need recall for downstream features, consider top_k=20 and use score_threshold to prune.

Output schema / structured response
- We return an ordered list of candidates with fields: doc_id, score, rerank_reason (short tokenized rationale when requested), and optional tool_call metadata for downstream feature extraction. Example: [{doc_id: 'd1', score: 0.87, rerank_reason: 'matches query entities'}].

Practical notes
- If CoreHealth decides to run embeddings later, we recommend redwood-embed-1 (512-d) for balance of CPU/GPU cost and retrieval accuracy.
- We'll provide a small evaluation notebook and the reranker-eval-plan.md attached.

I attached the eval plan and a short example snippet for the Python SDK showing how to call POST /v1/rank and consume scores.

Cheers,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
